valuation.method: Bank: tangible book value per common share (TBVPS) projected to the 12-month target date (Nov 2027) x P/TBV. Q3 2026 TBVPS $112.64 (reported 2026-10-13), grown at about 7%/yr (Q3 reported growth 7% y/y; ROTCE about 20% less payout of dividends and buybacks) to roughly $121 in Nov 2027. Steady-state check: P/TBV = (ROTCE - g)/(COE - g) = (20% - 6%)/(10.7% - 6%) = 3.0x. Cross-check: base TBVPS $121 x 3.0x = $363, about 15.8x FY2027 EPS of roughly $23 (analyst-style model assumption, not guidance). USD listing, no ADR conversion.

bear.driver: Credit cycle turns (card and CRE losses, leveraged finance/hedge fund stress), NII falls short of the roughly $107B ex-Markets 2027 central case, ROTCE about 15%, buybacks slow so TBVPS grows only about 4%.

base.driver: Management central case holds: 2027 NII ex-Markets about $107B, ROTCE about 20%, TBVPS compounding about 7% with steady buybacks and dividends.

bull.driver: Stronger IB/Markets and fee revenue, benign credit, ROTCE 21-22%, deregulation lowers capital requirements and lets buybacks accelerate.

valuation.implied_by_close: The close of $346.19 is 3.07x Q3 TBVPS of $112.64 and 2.86x base-case Nov 2027 TBVPS of $121. The recency-weighted named-analyst target (about $370) implies 3.06x base TBVPS, or TBVPS of about $123 at a constant 3.0x.
valuation.sensitivity: 0.1x of P/TBV moves the base target by $12.10 (3.5 pp of price return); a full turn is $121 (35 pp), so the base case is far more sensitive to the multiple than to TBVPS ($1 of TBVPS = $3).
valuation.watch_metric: Reported ROTCE (base case needs about 20%) and TBVPS growth (base needs about 7% y/y), together with card and CRE net charge-offs and the 2027 NII ex-Markets guide (about $107B).
valuation.next_disclosure: Q4 2026 earnings, expected about 2027-01-14 (provider estimate; confirm on the company IR calendar).

analyst_notes: Only 6 named analysts were sourced (of about 23 in the Yahoo aggregate, mean $373.48, range $312-$425), so the sample is partial and mixes post-Q3 calls (Oct 14-15: RBC, BofA, Citi, Truist) with July calls (Deutsche, HSBC). Named targets are $340-$400; Citi cut $360 to $350 while Truist rose $352 to $361, and none of the sampled Buy-rated names is below $370. The recency-weighted sample target of roughly $370 is about 2 pp above the $363 base case, equivalent to TBVPS of about $123 versus $121 at 3.0x, or about 3.06x versus 3.0x; the analysts' underlying assumptions are not known. Target horizons are not documented for any sampled firm, so none enter the weighted target. Other post-Q3 moves (Morgan Stanley $370 to $377 Equal-Weight, Baird $305 to $312 Neutral, Barclays $420 to $425 Overweight, UBS $395 to $400 Buy, Goldman $392 Buy) were reported without a verifiable analyst name and are omitted from individual histories. Truist's exact issue date (Oct 14) is inferred from the post-earnings roundup.
